examples.ko: 아버지가 벽에 못질을 해서 액자를 걸었어요.
examples.en: My father hammered a nail into the wall and hung the picture frame.
I can hear the sound of hammering from next door until late at night.
I'm clumsy at hammering nails, so I almost hurt my finger.

examples.ko: 못질 한 번 하는 데도 힘이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Even one round of nailing takes a lot of effort.

examples.ko: 못질 몇 번이면 의자가 다시 튼튼해져요.
examples.en: A few hammer blows and the chair will be sturdy again.

examples.ko: 주말에 아이와 같이 못질 연습을 했어요.
examples.en: On the weekend I practiced hammering nails with my child.

explain: '못을 박다'라고 풀어 말하기도 하지만, '못질'은 못을 박는 일 전체를 가볍게 가리켜요. '못질 소리', '못질이 서툴다'처럼 소리나 솜씨를 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: You can also say '못을 박다' (to drive a nail), but '못질' refers to the whole job of nailing in a casual way. It fits well when talking about the sound or skill, as in '못질 소리' or '못질이 서툴다'.

examples.en: I'm hammering a nail so I can hang a picture frame on the wall.
I nailed boards over the window to block it.

examples.ko: 아빠가 의자 옆에서 조심스럽게 못질하고 있어요.
examples.en: Dad is carefully hammering nails next to the chair.

examples.ko: 못질하다가 손가락을 망치로 쳐서 많이 아팠어요.
examples.en: I hit my finger with the hammer while nailing, and it really hurt.

examples.ko: 저는 혼자 못질해 본 적이 거의 없어요.
examples.en: I've hardly ever nailed anything by myself.
The wall is thin, so please don't hammer nails in here.

explain: '못을 박다'와 거의 같은 뜻이지만, '못질하다'는 한 번 박는 것보다 망치로 계속 두드리는 작업처럼 들려요. 주로 '~에 못질하다'처럼 박는 자리를 조사 '에'로 말해요.
explain_en: It's nearly the same as '못을 박다', but '못질하다' sounds more like ongoing work with a hammer than a single nail. The place you nail is usually marked with '에', as in '~에 못질하다'.

examples.en: I can't bear to throw away this stubby pencil, so I'm still using it.

examples.ko: 서랍 속에서 몽당연필 몇 자루가 나왔어요.
examples.en: A few stubby pencils turned up in the drawer.
My grandfather writes his diary with a stubby pencil.

examples.ko: 몽당연필에 볼펜 대를 끼워서 쓰면 편해요.
examples.en: It's easier to use a stubby pencil if you stick it into a pen casing.
When I was little, I used even stubby pencils with care.

examples.ko: 이 몽당연필은 너무 짧아서 잡기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This pencil stub is so short that it's hard to hold.

explain: 많이 써서 짧아진 연필을 말해요. 연필은 '자루'로 세고, 아껴 쓰는 모습이나 옛날 학용품 이야기를 할 때 잘 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a pencil worn short from use. Pencils are counted with '자루', and the word often comes up when talking about thrifty habits or old-fashioned school supplies.

examples.en: The trip I took without any plan was more fun.

examples.ko: 무계획이 편할 때도 있지만 오래 가면 불안해요.
examples.en: Having no plan is comfortable at times, but it gets worrying if it goes on too long.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 무계획 때문에 일정이 계속 밀렸어요.
examples.en: Our team's lack of planning kept pushing the schedule back.
This vacation, I simply have no plans at all.

examples.ko: 무계획인 사람과 여행하면 힘들 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Traveling with someone who never plans can be hard at times.
It was a day with almost no plan, but it was enjoyable.

explain: '무계획으로', '무계획이다'처럼 쓰고, 좋게도 나쁘게도 말할 수 있어요. '계획 없이'는 더 부드러운 일상 표현이고, '무계획'은 짧고 딱 잘라 말하는 느낌이에요. 반대는 '계획적'이에요.
explain_en: It's used as '무계획으로' or '무계획이다' and can sound positive or negative depending on context. '계획 없이' is the softer everyday phrasing, while '무계획' feels short and blunt. The opposite is '계획적'.

examples.en: Spinach is rich in minerals such as iron.

examples.ko: 무기질은 뼈와 이를 튼튼하게 해 줘요.
examples.en: Minerals keep your bones and teeth strong.

examples.ko: 땀을 많이 흘리면 무기질도 같이 빠져나가요.
examples.en: When you sweat a lot, minerals leave your body too.

examples.ko: 채소와 해조류로 무기질을 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can get minerals from vegetables and seaweed.

examples.ko: 비타민과 무기질 보충제를 챙겨 먹고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm taking vitamin and mineral supplements.

examples.ko: 무기질이 부족하면 쉽게 피곤해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lack minerals, you can get tired easily.

explain: 영양 이야기에서 '비타민'과 함께 '비타민과 무기질'처럼 자주 묶여요. 칼슘, 철분 같은 하나하나는 구체적으로 이름을 말하고, '무기질'은 그 전체를 묶어 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: In talk about nutrition it often pairs with vitamins, as in '비타민과 무기질'. People name specific ones like calcium or iron individually, and use '무기질' as the group name for them all.

examples.en: Among the applicants, I got through the interview without trouble.

examples.ko: 이번 시험은 큰 실수 없이 무난히 끝났어요.
examples.en: This exam ended smoothly, without any big mistakes.
I'm adjusting to the new school without any problems.

examples.ko: 준비를 많이 해서 발표를 무난히 마쳤어요.
examples.en: I prepared a lot, so I finished the presentation without trouble.

examples.ko: 이 정도 실력이면 무난히 합격할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this level of skill, you can pass without difficulty.
The moving preparations went more smoothly than I expected.

explain: '쉽게'와 비슷하지만 '큰 문제 없이 별 탈 없이'라는 느낌이 강해서 통과, 합격, 적응, 진행 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 형용사 '무난하다'는 '무난한 색', '무난한 선택'처럼 평범하고 안전하다는 뜻으로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It's close to '쉽게', but it stresses 'without any big problem', so it goes well with passing, adapting, and proceeding. The adjective '무난하다' is also often used for something plain and safe, as in '무난한 색' or '무난한 선택'.

examples.en: I'm really helpless when it comes to computers.
When the boss is incompetent, the team members suffer.

examples.ko: 처음 일할 때는 누구나 무능력해 보여요.
examples.en: Everyone looks incompetent when they first start working.
Don't blame yourself too much for being incompetent.
Calling someone an incompetent person is too harsh.
Just because you're bad at cooking doesn't mean you're incompetent.

explain: 사람을 평가하는 말이라서 다른 사람에게 직접 쓰면 세게 들려요. '일을 잘 못하다', '능력이 없다'가 더 부드러운 말이고, 반대말은 '유능하다'예요.
explain_en: Since it judges a person, saying it directly to someone sounds harsh. '일을 잘 못하다' or '능력이 없다' are softer, and the opposite is '유능하다'.

examples.ko: 무당벌레는 진딧물의 천적이라서 텃밭에 있으면 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Ladybugs are natural enemies of aphids, so they help if they are in your garden.
A ladybug landed on the back of my hand.
The child looked at the red ladybug with wonder.
A ladybug has black spots on its back.
A ladybug is slowly crawling across the leaf.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 무당벌레를 잡고 놀았어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I used to play by catching ladybugs.

explain: 곤충이라서 '한 마리, 두 마리'처럼 '마리'로 세요. 진딧물을 먹기 때문에 텃밭이나 농사 이야기에서는 반가운 벌레로 말해요.
explain_en: It's an insect, so you count it with '마리', as in '한 마리, 두 마리'. Because it eats aphids, people talk about it as a welcome bug in gardens and farming.

examples.en: The blade has gone dull, so it doesn't cut well.

examples.ko: 매일 시끄러운 소리를 들었더니 소리에 무뎌졌어요.
examples.en: After hearing loud noise every day, I've grown numb to it.
As time passes, even sadness gradually dulls.
If you go through something again and again, you tend to become numb to the pain.
When the pencil lead gets blunt, you have to sharpen it again.

examples.ko: 요즘은 칭찬을 들어도 마음이 무뎌진 것 같아요.
examples.en: These days, even when I'm praised, my heart feels numb.

explain: 칼, 연필처럼 날카로운 물건에도 쓰고, 감각이나 감정이 둔해질 때도 써요. 감정에 쓸 때는 '~에 무뎌지다'처럼 무엇에 익숙해져서 느낌이 약해졌는지를 '에'로 말해요. 반대 느낌은 '날카로워지다'예요.
explain_en: It's used for sharp things like knives and pencils, and also when senses or feelings grow dull. For feelings, you mark what you've gotten used to with '에', as in '~에 무뎌지다'. The opposite feeling is '날카로워지다'.

examples.ko: 공원에서 자전거를 타다가 넘어져서 무르팍이 까졌어요.
examples.en: I fell while riding a bike in the park and scraped my knee.
The child has a bandage on their knee.

examples.ko: 할머니는 비가 오면 무르팍을 자꾸 주무르세요.
examples.en: When it rains, my grandmother keeps rubbing her knees.
I hurt the area below my knee while exercising.
I bought a skirt that comes down to the knee.
The child sat on Dad's knee.

explain: '무릎'을 편하게 말하는 구어체예요. 가족이나 친구와 이야기할 때, 특히 아이가 넘어져서 다친 이야기에 자주 어울려요. 공손한 자리나 글에서는 '무릎'을 쓰세요.
explain_en: It's a casual, spoken way of saying '무릎'. It suits chats with family and friends, especially stories about a child falling and getting hurt. In polite settings or writing, use '무릎'.

examples.en: I mixed dried radish strips with seasoning to make a side dish.
The dried radish my mother sent me is delicious.
Dried radish is chewy, so it's nice to bite into.
I packed seasoned dried radish as a side dish in my lunchbox.

examples.ko: 무말랭이도 먼저 물에 살짝 불려야 해요.
examples.en: You also need to soak dried radish in water for a bit first.
I bought a bag of dried radish at the mart.

explain: 무를 길게 썰어 말린 것이고, 보통 물에 불려서 양념에 무쳐 먹어요. 그렇게 만든 반찬은 '무말랭이 무침'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It's radish cut into strips and dried, and it's usually soaked in water and then seasoned. The side dish made this way is called '무말랭이 무침'.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 삼십 년째 무사고 운전자예요.
examples.en: My father has been an accident-free driver for thirty years.
This year too, we finished operating without any accidents.
At a construction site, having no accidents is most important.

examples.ko: 택시 기사님이 십 년 무사고라고 자랑하셨어요.
examples.en: The taxi driver boasted that he'd had no accidents in ten years.
I'm glad we recorded zero accidents again this month.

examples.ko: 무사고 소풍을 위해 안전 교육을 받았어요.
examples.en: We had safety training for an accident-free field trip.

explain: '무사고 운전', '무사고 기록'처럼 운전이나 작업장 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 반대는 '사고'이고, 사람이 다치지 않고 잘 지냈다는 뜻의 '무사하다'와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It often appears in phrases like '무사고 운전' and '무사고 기록', in talk about driving or workplaces. The opposite is '사고', and it is a different word from '무사하다', which means someone came through safe and sound.

examples.en: Things like stones and rocks are non-living things.

examples.ko: 아이들은 무생물에도 이름을 붙여 주곤 해요.
examples.en: Children often give names even to inanimate objects.

examples.ko: 무생물과 생물의 차이를 수업 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned the difference between living and non-living things in class.

examples.ko: 바위 같은 무생물은 스스로 자라지 못해요.
examples.en: Non-living things like rocks can't grow on their own.

examples.ko: 책상 같은 무생물을 사람처럼 말하면 재미있어요.
examples.en: It's funny to talk about inanimate things like a desk as if they were people.

examples.ko: 이 퀴즈는 생물인지 무생물인지 맞히는 거예요.
examples.en: This quiz is about guessing whether something is living or non-living.

explain: 반대말은 '생물'이고, 과학 수업이나 퀴즈에서 두 말을 짝으로 자주 말해요. 일상에서는 '사물'이라고도 하지만 '사물'에는 생물/무생물을 나누는 느낌이 없어요.
explain_en: The opposite is '생물', and the two are often paired in science class and quizzes. In daily talk people also say '사물' (thing), but it doesn't carry the living versus non-living distinction.

examples.en: That employee is too careless toward customers.
We got a complaint because of the half-hearted attitude.
I did my homework carelessly and got scolded by my teacher.
My friend's reply was so perfunctory that I felt hurt.

examples.ko: 무성의하다는 말을 들으면 기분이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel bad when I'm told I'm being half-hearted.

examples.ko: 무성의해 보이지 않게 인사라도 제대로 하세요.
examples.en: At least greet people properly so you don't look half-hearted.

explain: 일이나 말에 정성과 마음을 쏟지 않은 태도를 나무랄 때 써요. '대충 하다'와 비슷하지만, '무성의하다'는 상대에게 예의가 없다는 느낌까지 있어서 더 비판적으로 들려요. 반대는 '성의 있다'예요.
explain_en: You use it to criticize a lack of effort and care in work or words. It is similar to '대충 하다', but '무성의하다' also suggests a lack of respect for the other person, so it sounds more critical. The opposite is '성의 있다'.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 정당 없이 무소속으로 출마했어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker ran as an independent, without a party.
An independent candidate won the election.

examples.ko: 저는 어느 동아리에도 속하지 않은 무소속이에요.
examples.en: I'm unaffiliated, not belonging to any club.

examples.ko: 무소속의 입장에서 두 당의 의견을 들었어요.
examples.en: From an independent's standpoint, I listened to both parties' views.

examples.ko: 그는 팀을 떠나 한동안 무소속 신세였어요.
examples.en: He left the team and was without a team for a while.
Since I'm independent, I don't take anyone's side.

explain: 선거와 정치 뉴스에서 '무소속 후보', '무소속 의원'처럼 가장 많이 나와요. 스포츠에서 소속 팀이 없는 선수에게도 쓰고, 반대는 '소속'이에요.
explain_en: It shows up most in election and political news, as in '무소속 후보' and '무소속 의원'. It's also used in sports for a player with no team, and the opposite is '소속'.

examples.en: He is too insensitive to other people's feelings.
I was hurt by one thoughtless remark.
My friend carelessly mentioned my weak point.

examples.ko: 저는 무신경해서 그런지 소음에도 잘 자요.
examples.en: Maybe because I'm not sensitive, I sleep well even with noise.

examples.ko: 무신경하다는 말을 들었지만 일부러 그런 건 아니에요.
examples.en: I was told I'm insensitive, but I didn't do it on purpose.

examples.ko: 무신경해 보이는 사람도 속은 여릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even someone who seems insensitive can be soft inside.

explain: 남의 감정이나 주변 상황을 잘 알아채지 못하는 사람이나 말에 써서 보통 비판하는 느낌이 있어요. 자기 자신에게 쓰면 '둔감하다'처럼 소음, 냄새 등에 잘 반응하지 않는다는 편한 뜻이 되기도 해요. 반대는 '예민하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes a person or remark that fails to notice others' feelings or the situation around them, and it usually sounds critical. When used about yourself, it can also mean you're not bothered by noise or smells, like '둔감하다'. The opposite is '예민하다'.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 십 년 넘게 무역업을 하고 있어요.
examples.en: My uncle has been in the trade business for over ten years.
I was interested in the trade business, so I went into economics.
The trade business is greatly affected by exchange rates.
My father's trade business has gotten busy lately.
It's a small company, but it succeeded greatly in trade.

examples.ko: 무역업 하는 친구가 해외 출장을 자주 가요.
examples.en: My friend in the trade business often goes on overseas trips.

explain: '무역업을 하다', '무역업에 종사하다'처럼 직업이나 사업을 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '무역 회사에 다니다', '수출입 일을 하다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: It's used for a job or business, as in '무역업을 하다' or '무역업에 종사하다'. In daily talk people also say '무역 회사에 다니다' or '수출입 일을 하다'.

examples.ko: 합창단이 먼저 노래했고 이어 무용단이 무대에 올랐어요.
examples.en: The choir sang first, and then the dance company stepped onto the stage.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 무용단은 연습이 정말 힘들어요.
examples.en: Our school's dance troupe has really tough practices.
My older sister is active in the city dance company.
I booked tickets for the dance company's performance in advance.

examples.ko: 그 무용단의 새 작품이 아주 좋았어요.
examples.en: That dance company's new piece was really good.

examples.ko: 저도 대학교 때 무용단에 들어가 보고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I also wanted to join a dance troupe in college.

explain: 춤을 추는 사람들이 모인 단체예요. '합창단', '극단'처럼 '-단'이 붙은 말과 같이 공연 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It's a group of dancers who perform together. It appears in talk about performances alongside other '-단' words like '합창단' and '극단'.

examples.en: When I'm nervous, I bite my nails without realizing it.

examples.ko: 꿈에는 무의식이 드러난다고 하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say the unconscious shows up in dreams.

examples.ko: 무의식 속에 남은 기억이 가끔 떠올라요.
examples.en: A memory left in my subconscious sometimes comes back.

examples.ko: 그 말은 무의식에서 나온 거라 저도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: That remark came from my subconscious, so I didn't realize it either.

examples.ko: 나쁜 습관은 무의식으로 반복될 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Bad habits are often repeated unconsciously.

examples.ko: 무의식을 연구하는 심리학 책을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading a psychology book about the unconscious.

explain: 자기도 모르게 하는 행동이나 마음속 깊은 곳을 말할 때 써요. 기절해서 정신을 잃은 상태는 보통 '의식을 잃다', '의식이 없다'라고 말하고, 반대말은 '의식'이에요.
explain_en: It's used for actions you do without realizing, or for the deep part of the mind. For passing out, people usually say '의식을 잃다' or '의식이 없다', and the opposite word is '의식'.

examples.en: It was an unconscious action, so I don't know the reason either.
When I'm nervous, I shake my leg without meaning to.
It was an automatic reaction, so I couldn't help it.
Speech habits are unconscious, so they're hard to change.

examples.ko: 사람은 무의식적으로 비슷한 사람을 고르곤 해요.
examples.en: People tend to pick similar people without realizing it.
Everything I did was unconscious.

explain: '무의식적으로 손톱을 깨물다'처럼 자기도 모르게 하는 행동에 써요. '의식적'은 알고 하는 것으로 반대예요. 일상에서는 '저도 모르게'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It fits actions done without noticing, as in '무의식적으로 손톱을 깨물다' (bite one's nails unconsciously). Its opposite, '의식적', means doing something knowingly. In daily talk, '저도 모르게' is more common.

examples.ko: 냉장고를 사려고 무이자 할부 행사를 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm waiting for an interest-free installment event to buy a refrigerator.

examples.ko: 이 카드는 석 달 무이자로 결제할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With this card you can pay interest-free over three months.
It's interest-free, so I decided to buy it without worry.

examples.ko: 이 상품은 무이자가 아니라서 수수료가 있어요.
examples.en: This item isn't interest-free, so there is a fee.
I thought it was interest-free, but a fee was added.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 무이자 육 개월 할부가 돼요.
examples.en: That store offers six-month interest-free installments.

explain: 쇼핑에서는 거의 '무이자 할부'로 나와요. 반대는 '유이자'보다 '이자가 붙다'처럼 풀어서 말하는 경우가 더 많아요. 광고에는 '수수료'가 따로 붙는 경우도 있으니 조건을 꼭 확인하세요.
explain_en: In shopping it almost always appears as '무이자 할부' (interest-free installments). For the opposite, people more often say '이자가 붙다' than a single word. Ads may still add a separate fee, so check the conditions.

examples.en: A new unmanned shop opened in our neighborhood.
At an unmanned shop, you have to pay by yourself.
Late at night I dropped by a self-service shop and bought ice cream.

examples.ko: 저는 무인점포를 이용하는 게 아직 어색해요.
examples.en: I still feel awkward using unmanned shops.

examples.ko: 무인점포 앞에서 사용 방법을 한참 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read the instructions for a long while in front of the unmanned shop.
The store that was run as an unmanned shop has closed.

explain: 직원 없이 손님이 직접 고르고 계산하는 가게예요. '무인 카페', '무인 세탁소'처럼 '무인'을 붙인 말과 함께 써요. 반대는 '유인 점포'보다 그냥 '일반 가게'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It's a shop where customers choose and pay on their own without staff. It goes with other '무인' words like '무인 카페' and '무인 세탁소'. For the opposite, people simply say '일반 가게' (regular shop).

examples.ko: 무조건적인 비난보다 해결 방법을 찾는 게 먼저예요.
examples.en: Finding a solution comes before blind criticism.

examples.ko: 저는 부모님의 무조건적 사랑을 받고 자랐어요.
examples.en: I grew up receiving my parents' unconditional love.
Think first rather than following blindly.
His support is unconditional, so it always feels reassuring.

examples.ko: 무조건적인 양보가 항상 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Giving in unconditionally isn't always a good thing.

examples.ko: 무조건적으로 반대만 하면 대화가 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you just oppose everything unconditionally, you can't have a conversation.

explain: '무조건'이 일상에서 더 자주 쓰이고, '무조건적'은 글이나 토론에서 '무조건적인 사랑', '무조건적으로'처럼 쓰는 편이에요. 사랑이나 응원에는 좋은 뜻이지만 비난, 복종, 반대에는 '앞뒤 안 따지고'라는 부정적인 느낌이 돼요.
explain_en: '무조건' is more common in daily talk, while '무조건적' tends to appear in writing and discussion, as in '무조건적인 사랑' and '무조건적으로'. With love or support it's positive, but with criticism, obedience, or opposition it sounds negative, like 'without thinking it through'.

examples.en: I got athlete's foot, so I'm putting medicine on it.

examples.ko: 무좀은 따뜻하고 습한 곳에서 잘 번져요.
examples.en: Athlete's foot spreads easily in warm, humid places.

examples.ko: 무좀 때문에 발가락 사이가 계속 가려워요.
examples.en: Because of athlete's foot, the area between my toes keeps itching.

examples.ko: 무좀에 걸린 가족과 수건을 따로 써야 해요.
examples.en: You should use separate towels from a family member with athlete's foot.
I'd had athlete's foot for a long time, so I went to the hospital.
After applying the athlete's foot medicine, it got much better.

explain: '무좀에 걸리다', '무좀이 생기다'처럼 말하고, 약은 '무좀약'이라고 해요. 증상은 주로 가려움이라서 '발이 가렵다'와 같이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: People say '무좀에 걸리다' or '무좀이 생기다', and the medicine is called '무좀약'. Itching is the typical symptom, so it often comes up together with '발이 가렵다'.

examples.en: The exit was narrow, so the scene fell into disorder.

examples.ko: 도로의 무질서가 사고를 부를 수 있어요.
examples.en: Disorder on the road can lead to accidents.

examples.ko: 제 방은 지금 무질서 그 자체예요.
examples.en: My room is complete disorder right now.
To reduce disorder, announcements are needed.

examples.ko: 겉보기에 무질서처럼 보여도 나름의 규칙이 있어요.
examples.en: It may look like disorder on the surface, but it has its own rules.

examples.ko: 무질서와 혼란 속에서 사람들이 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: People got lost amid the disorder and confusion.

explain: 규칙이나 순서 없이 어지러운 상태를 말하고, 반대는 '질서'예요. '질서를 지키다'와 짝을 이루어 '질서와 무질서'처럼 같이 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a messy state with no rules or order, and the opposite is '질서'. It pairs with '질서를 지키다' and is also said together as '질서와 무질서'.

examples.ko: 아이 방이 너무 무질서해서 찾을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: The kid's room is so disordered that I can't find anything.
Seeing a disorderly street makes me uncomfortable.
The market is especially chaotic today.

examples.ko: 책상 위가 무질서하지만 저는 다 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: My desk is a mess, but I can find everything.
The line was stretched out in a disorderly way.

examples.ko: 무질서하다고 느낄 때는 먼저 정리부터 해요.
examples.en: When it feels disordered, I start by tidying up.

explain: 방이나 책상이 어지러운 것은 '어지럽다', '지저분하다'가 더 일상적이에요. '무질서하다'는 사람들이 줄을 안 서거나 규칙이 없는 거리·현장처럼 질서가 없는 상황에 더 잘 어울려요. 반대는 '질서 있다', '정돈되다'예요.
explain_en: For a messy room or desk, '어지럽다' and '지저분하다' are more everyday. '무질서하다' fits situations without order, like streets or scenes where people ignore lines and rules. The opposites are '질서 있다' and '정돈되다'.

examples.en: I blanch spinach and toss it with sesame oil.
My mother is seasoning bean sprouts.

examples.ko: 나물을 무칠 때는 양념을 조금씩 넣어요.
examples.en: When I season vegetables, I add the seasoning little by little.
I salted the cucumber and then mixed it with chili powder.

examples.ko: 간장과 참기름에 무치면 간단한 반찬이 돼요.
examples.en: Tossed in soy sauce and sesame oil, it becomes an easy side dish.

examples.ko: 손으로 살살 무쳐야 나물이 부서지지 않아요.
examples.en: You need to toss it gently by hand so the greens don't break.

explain: 나물이나 채소에 양념을 넣고 섞는 요리를 말해요. 김치처럼 속을 가득 버무릴 때는 '버무리다'를 많이 쓰고, 밥에 섞을 때는 '비비다'를 써요. 소리가 비슷한 '사무치다'는 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It's for mixing seasoning into vegetables or greens. For coating something thoroughly like kimchi filling, '버무리다' is common, and for mixing with rice you use '비비다'. The similar-sounding '사무치다' is a completely different word.

examples.en: The seasoned bellflower root suits my taste perfectly.

examples.ko: 식당에서 나물 무침을 한 접시 더 시켰어요.
examples.en: I ordered one more plate of seasoned greens at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 무침은 양념이 중요해서 간을 잘 봐야 해요.
examples.en: For seasoned dishes the seasoning matters, so you need to taste it well.

examples.ko: 어머니의 무침 맛은 아무도 못 따라가요.
examples.en: No one can match the taste of my mother's seasoned dishes.
I added a little vinegar to this seasoned dish.

examples.ko: 밥이랑 무침만 있어도 한 끼가 충분해요.
examples.en: Rice and a seasoned side dish alone make a good meal.

explain: 보통 '오이무침', '콩나물무침'처럼 재료 이름 뒤에 붙여 써요. 주로 반찬이고, 같은 재료로 만든 '볶음'이나 '조림'과는 만드는 방법이 달라요.
explain_en: It's usually attached to an ingredient, as in '오이무침' or '콩나물무침'. It's mostly a side dish, and it is made differently from '볶음' (stir-fried) or '조림' (braised) dishes with the same ingredient.

examples.ko: 무턱대고 사지 말고 먼저 후기를 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just buy it blindly; read the reviews first.

examples.ko: 그는 무턱대고 저를 찾아와서 돈을 빌려 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: He showed up out of the blue and asked me to lend him money.

examples.ko: 길을 모르면 무턱대고 가지 말고 지도를 보세요.
examples.en: If you don't know the way, don't just head off; look at a map.
If you get angry without thinking first, misunderstandings arise.

examples.ko: 준비도 없이 무턱대고 창업하는 건 위험해요.
examples.en: Starting a business recklessly without preparation is risky.
The child threw a tantrum for no reason, and it was awkward.

explain: 앞뒤를 생각하거나 준비하지 않고 행동할 때 써서 보통 '그러지 마세요'라는 충고와 같이 나와요. '무턱대고 ~하지 마세요'가 아주 자주 쓰는 말투예요. 비슷한 '무작정'은 '계획 없이 그냥'의 뜻이라 꼭 나쁘게만 들리지는 않아요.
explain_en: You use it for acting without thinking ahead or preparing, so it often comes with advice not to. '무턱대고 ~하지 마세요' is a very common pattern. The similar '무작정' means 'just, with no plan', and doesn't always sound negative.

examples.ko: 문고리가 헐거워서 문이 잘 안 잠겨요.
examples.en: The door handle is loose, so the door doesn't lock well.
I grabbed the doorknob and slowly opened the door.
I hung my bag on the doorknob.
The doorknob is placed too high for a child.
I went to the hardware store to swap in a new door handle.

examples.ko: 문고리는 돌려도 열리지 않아서 열쇠를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The door wouldn't open even when I turned the handle, so I looked for the key.

explain: 문을 열고 닫을 때 잡는 부분이에요. 일상에서는 '문손잡이'나 '손잡이'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: It's the part you hold to open and close a door. In daily talk, '문손잡이' or just '손잡이' are used in a similar way.

examples.en: In a civilized society, obeying the law is the basics.
In a civilized society, people should treat each other with courtesy.
As members of a civilized society, we have responsibilities.
Even civilized societies have many unsolved problems.

examples.ko: 이런 일이 문명사회에서 일어나다니 믿을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't believe something like this happens in a civilized society.
As civilized society developed, environmental problems grew too.

explain: 뉴스나 토론에서 '문명사회에서 어떻게 이럴 수 있어요?'처럼 어떤 행동을 비판할 때 자주 나와요. 일상 대화보다는 조금 딱딱한 말이라서 글이나 발표에서 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: In news and debates it often appears when criticizing something, as in '문명사회에서 어떻게 이럴 수 있어요?' It's a bit formal compared with daily conversation, so it suits writing and presentations better.
